quote.text: The supreme ideal does not call for any external aids. It is homegrown, wholly self-developed. Once it starts looking outside itself for any part of itself it is on the way to being dominated by fortune.
quote.author: Seneca
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood:
    • True growth in both parent and child emerges from within, nurtured by self-discipline and personal reflection.
    • Relying on external validation or shortcuts in parenting may lead one astray, undermining the organic development of resilience and character in a child.
  • Leadership:
    • A leader's strength is found not in external accolades but in cultivating a deep, intrinsic sense of purpose and virtue.
    • By focusing on internal ideals rather than the whims of fortune or external approval, a leader can steer their team with unwavering consistency and integrity.
  • Product Management:
    • Crafting an outstanding product stems from a vision that is cultivated internally; it is the result of deep insight and understanding of core values rather than fleeting market trends.
    • When a product manager relies solely on external influences, the product risks losing its identity, making it vulnerable to capricious market forces instead of building a loyal following.
